For coding agents (Claude Code or any other) and the people directing them. It says what the system is, where to change what, how to verify, and what goes wrong. It is agent-agnostic; the worked example uses Claude Code.

## Mental model in six lines

1. Neo4j holds a graph. The GraphQL API is **generated** from `grandstack-server/schema/schema.graphql`; there are no resolvers to edit.
2. The web app (`grandstack-web`) asks that API for data using operations written with `graphql()` and typed by `npm run codegen` against the live schema.
3. State a user may want to share (filters) lives in the URL.
4. Sample data comes from a versioned Cypher seed; titles and names are unique keys.
5. Writes go through generated mutations; a server plugin keeps stored film counts correct.
6. The default stack has **no authentication**, and the app can edit and delete everything. An opt-in setup (`compose.auth.yaml`, the `grandstack-auth` repo) adds login, a gateway and row-level rules; `grandstack-web` is intentionally not part of it.

## Notes on setup

`npm ci` prints `npm warn install-scripts ... approve` warnings; they are harmless. The package versions in `package.json` match the git tags.

## Where to change what

| You want to... | Change | Then run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add or change a field, type or relationship | `grandstack-server/schema/schema.graphql` (+ seed if it needs data) | server checks, then `npm run codegen` in the web repo |
| Change the sample data | `grandstack-server/seed/movies.cypher`, bump `// seed-version` | restart the server |
| Add a computed field | `@cypher` in the schema | server checks |
| Change server behaviour or add a setting | `grandstack-server/src/` | server checks |
| Show a field, add a filter, page or form | `grandstack-web/src/` | web checks |
| Change look and feel | `grandstack-web/src/theme/tokens.css`, `src/styles.css` | web checks |
| Change ports, services or settings of the stack | `grandstack/compose.yaml` | `docker compose up --build` |
| Change who can do what (roles, permissions, rules) | `grandstack-auth` (`gateway/rules.ts`, `schema/auth.graphql`, `keycloak/grandstack-realm.json`) | its smoke script and tests |
| Add login to a front end | follow `grandstack-auth/docs/exercise-add-auth-to-grandstack-web.md` in your own copy | its acceptance check |
| Use your own dataset | see [build your own app](/docs/grandstack/build-your-own-app/) | |

Each repository has recipes for the common changes: `docs/recipes.md` in `grandstack-server` and in `grandstack-web`. Start there.

## Start the stack

```sh
cd grandstack
cp .env.example .env      # once
docker compose up --build # web :3000, GraphQL :4000/graphql, Neo4j browser :7474

# with login (development only): gateway :4000, Keycloak :8081, auth demo client :3001
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.auth.yaml up --build

# with federation (Wikipedia summaries on films and people; needs internet): gateway :4000, subgraphs :4001 and :4010
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.federation.yaml up --build

# with an MCP server for agents: http://localhost:4100/mcp (read-only; AGENTS_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true to write)
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.agents.yaml up --build
```

Wait for the server log line `GraphQL ready at http://localhost:4000/graphql`. Use `docker compose down -v` to reset the data to the sample.

## Verification checklist

Run what matches the repo you changed. All of it must pass before you call a change done.

```sh
# grandstack-server
npm run lint && npm test && npm run schema:check && npm run docs:check

# grandstack-web (codegen needs a server running with the schema you want; it reads
# GRAPHQL_URL, default http://localhost:4000/graphql)
npm run codegen && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run docs:check

# grandstack-web browser checks (freshly seeded stack; creates and deletes ZZ-prefixed test data)
npm run e2e

# grandstack-auth: unit tests, then (with the auth stack running) the token-level and browser checks
(cd gateway && npm ci && npm test && npm run typecheck)
(cd client && npm ci && npm test && npm run typecheck)
npm ci && npm run docs:check && npm run smoke && npm run e2e

# grandstack-agents: tests and types need no stack; live needs the open stack, auth:check the auth stack
npm ci && npm test && npm run typecheck && npm run docs:check && npm run live

# grandstack-federation: tests and types need no stack; smoke needs the federation stack and internet
npm ci && npm test && npm run typecheck && npm run docs:check && npm run smoke
```

`schema:check` needs a git checkout with the schema committed at `HEAD` (commit the baseline before you edit). `docs:check` fails until you have run `npm run docs:schema` after a schema change; commit the regenerated reference.

For a server schema change also check the live API, for example:

```sh
curl -s localhost:4000/graphql -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"{ movies(limit:1) { title rating } }"}'
```

Do not claim a UI change works from a build alone: open the page (or use `npm run e2e` screenshots with `OUT=dir`) and look.

## Using the API without writing code

The endpoint accepts introspection, so an agent can discover the schema itself:

```sh
curl -s localhost:4000/graphql -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"{ __schema { queryType { fields { name description } } mutationType { fields { name } } } }"}'
```

Every type and field defined in the schema has a description (lint enforces it), and `grandstack-server/docs/schema-reference.md` lists them. The generated queries and mutations (`movies`, `createMovies`, ...) have no descriptions but follow a fixed naming pattern per type (see that repo's `docs/schema-guide.md`). Filters look like `movies(where: { rating: { gte: 8 }, genres: { some: { name: { in: ["Drama"] } } } })`; writes are covered in `grandstack-server/docs/mutations.md`. An MCP server that runs GraphQL statements is available with `compose.agents.yaml` (port 4100, read-only by default); see `grandstack-agents` (`README.md`, `docs/direct-graphql.md`). How well an agent does depends on how the type definitions are written; see `grandstack-agents` `docs/schema-design-for-agents.md`.

## Gotchas that cost time

- **Every type, field and argument needs a description** in the schema, or lint fails.
- **Types need `@node`** (v7). New Neo4j directives need a stub in `grandstack-server/tooling/neo4j-directives.graphql`.
- **Scalar updates are `{ set: value }`.** A bare value fails validation.
- **Relationship updates must be diffs.** "Disconnect all, then connect" in one mutation removes the new links, because the disconnect runs last. `buildUpdateInput` in the web repo shows the right shape.
- **`contains` is case-sensitive.** The web app matches several casings.
- **Seed changes need a bumped `// seed-version`.** Cypher map keys are bare words.
- **Operation names must be unique across the web app**, and variables used in non-null positions must be declared non-null.
- **Keep `graphql` on 16.x** in both repos. Pin exact dependency versions.
- **Do not add `@neo4j-ndl/*`** to the web app: it is GPL-3.0 and the repo is Apache-2.0.
- **`VITE_GRAPHQL_URL` is fixed at build time** and must be reachable from the browser; the server's `CORS_ORIGIN` must allow the web origin.
- **Text inputs that write to the URL need local state and a debounce**, or fast typing drops characters.
- **Never expose the stack publicly.** The default stack has no auth, and the auth setup is development-only (demo realm, known passwords, plain HTTP).
- **Auth:** a new mutation must be added to `MUTATION_PERMISSIONS` in `grandstack-auth/gateway/rules.ts` or the gateway refuses it; server rules must be `filter` (not `validate`) and avoid `DateTime` (both need APOC); `AUTH_ISSUER` is the browser-facing URL while `AUTH_JWKS_URL` is the container-reachable one; realm edits need a recreated Keycloak. More in `grandstack-auth/AGENTS.md`.
- **Commit generated files when they change:** `grandstack-web/src/graphql/generated/` and `grandstack-server/docs/schema-reference.md`.

## Keep the docs true

Docs live next to the code they describe. When you change behaviour, update the doc in the same change: environment variables in `docs/configuration.md` (server), routes and folder map in `docs/architecture.md` (web), versions in [versioning and releases](/docs/grandstack/versioning-and-releases/). `npm run docs:check` fails on a stale schema reference (server) or a broken relative link (all repos).

## Example: asking Claude Code to make a change

Open Claude Code in the folder that holds the repositories, then give it a task and point it at the docs:

> Add a `country` field to Movie and show it on the movie page. Follow `grandstack/docs/agents.md` and the recipes in each repo's `docs/recipes.md`. Run the checks before you say it is done.

A good run follows the recipes: add the described field to the schema, lint and check for breaking changes, regenerate the schema reference, restart the server, add `country` to the movie query in the web app, run `npm run codegen`, render it in `MovieDetail.tsx`, then run the checks above and look at the page. Any other agent can follow the same documents.
